notes: v1.8.0 is the full-bleed layout and gate-movement patch. (1) The shell stops all width clamping: .app-shell is 100% viewport width at every resolution (the v1.6.0-era min(100% - Npx, 2000/2320px) caps and small-screen width overrides are gone), and both sticky bars (.topbar, .commandbar) plus .main span the viewport edge to edge with a shared --gutter-x edge inset (clamp(16px, 1.8vw, 34px) under safe-area max()) carried inside the bars, so no screen shows book margins and the top bar no longer reads as a fixed-width row. No route, palette, or interaction changes. (2) The landing gate gains real movement: three satellites orbit the tower mark on counter-rotating rings (.go), three light streaks cross the sky on long cycles (.gstr), and the cursor drives --gx/--gy parallax (gate core/stage shift toward the pointer, aurora blobs counter-shift) from a passive pointermove listener skipped under prefers-reduced-motion; all new pieces are display:none in the reduced-motion and print states and the existing global animation freeze covers them. (3) Encoding hygiene: index.html and styles.css carried double-encoded characters from an earlier PowerShell round-trip (BOM + mojibake em dashes/middots, one user-visible in the footer separator content: property) - both repaired to clean UTF-8 without BOM; app.js and all docs were already clean. Byte ceilings unchanged and unbreached: index.html 74,131/78,000, styles.css 185,989/186,000, app.js 280,775/286,000, brotli 108,376/112,000, gzip 122,244/130,000, total 542,310/556,000. v1.7.0 lab results remain recorded in the performanceException entry below.

performanceException.note: Performance exception originated in v1.1.0. Fresh Lighthouse re-measurements per release live in PERFORMANCE.md: accessibility 1.0 and CLS 0.000 hold on all tabs and FCP/LCP pass everywhere. TBT exceeded the gate through v1.2.0, passed on all three audited tabs in the v1.3.0 release run (113/200/151 ms), passed Overview and Guidance in the v1.4.0 (104-177/132-137 ms) and v1.5.0 (99/170 ms) and v1.5.1 (142/140 ms) runs while NOC read 219-350/250/249 ms inside the documented range, and passed on all three tabs in the v1.6.0 (122/161/180 ms) and v1.7.0 (154/157/160 ms) release runs and again in the v1.8.0 release run (94/172/154 ms). In v1.7.0 the Phase 4 perf lab retired the interaction-probe side: Guidance first activation passes its 750 ms gate (lab p75 336-408 ms) and the warm tab-switch gate was raised 200 -> 400 ms p75 with user approval on 2026-11-13 after the lab showed an honest optimized floor of 264-368 ms p75 at 4x CPU (experiment ledger and engine-cost decomposition in PERFORMANCE.md); table virtualization stays open as the remaining structural lever. The documented NOC TBT variance range (171-492 ms) and the same-day v1.3.0 control builds (384/229 ms with less NOC content) remain the machine-state evidence for that exception. v1.8.0 (full-bleed shell) A/B'd against the v1.7.0 zip build back-to-back on the same machine: no regression (v1.8.0 240-360 ms p75 across runs including a best-ever 240; v1.7.0 312-368 ms on the same windows); day-to-day lab spread is wider than the +-10% repeatability spec when the machine is not quiet (one v1.8.0 run read 408 ms p75 while background processes were active), so the release gate verdict is taken from quiet-machine runs.
